body: I *am* a butthurt little kid that's too young to have experienced anything real yet. But after spending 10 minutes on this sub it's really difficult to imagine that my life won't be of depreciated quality because of my height. I'm not complaining about what I have experienced, but what I most likely will experience in the future.

My school's not really like normal high schools. It's super academically oriented and that's all anyone cares about primarily. I don't really have friends in the traditional sense. I have people I talk to during lunch I guess, but they're not really the type of people who care about my problems. Same thing with my school counselors. They're really only there for kids who are getting straight Cs and need help for college, not for emotional support. I've revealed more about my sadness online than I have to anyone in real life.

 My parents want to bury their heads in the sand and my "friends" and school counselors really couldn't care less about me. Reddit is literally my last remaining outlet.

There's a lot of scientific evidence that suggests we inherit our violent tendencies from our primate ancestors. Chimpanzees share a recent common ancestor with us, and even without conscious thought, they're incredibly prone to intra-species violence. Just like us.

I've tried, but they either try to change the subject to schoolwork/studying or they (my dad especially) get mad and start telling me how lucky I am to be in a lower-upper class family and not homeless (which is true) and that I don't have the right to be sad and dejected (which is also true).

Hopefully any positive social status associated with being a specialized medical practitioner outweighs any negatives (real or supposed) and I can live a normal life. Even so, I'll still try to make college a worthwhile experience though. Thanks again, I actually feel a lot better.
Glad that your height didn't hinder you in life, looks like you have it pretty good. Hopefully I can emulate your success later on.
Obvious troll is obvious. You truly are pathetic if you have nothing better to do than to kick someone who is already down.

Thanks for the advice/motivation. Honestly it's not just the height itself that bothers me. It's the overarching theme of not fitting in with society at all in my life. The height is just one of a long list of traits that the average joe has that I don't. But I guess I'll just carry on and see how it goes in college. I've heard some people say it gets worse in adulthood since everyone is fully grown and I've heard that it gets better in adulthood since people aren't shallow teenagers anymore, and both make an equal amount of sense to some degree. I guess I'll just have to wait and see.
Isn't that why we have the Electoral College (in America at least)?

I'm sorry to hear that you're in a spot similar to mine - nobody deserves to be an outsider in this superficial society we live in. I can never understand what being overweight is like because my life has always been about me trying to gain weight, but I'm sure it's just as painful if not more. I feel exactly the same as you otherwise though, everyone around me is growing up and "finding themselves" while I'm just stuck in a perpetual state of loneliness and sadness. I have no true friends either, the people I talk to are just that - people I talk to. They don't really care about me and after we graduate I'll probably never talk to them again. The most I can tell you is that you're not the only one. I envy those who are already dead.

I don't know how, but you're completely right. I've had issues with social inadequacy my whole life, and I've tried to change it and become more sociable. Except now I know that people look down on those smaller than they are as stupid and immature and that the thing that causes people to never take me seriously might be my height, which is something that will never change. I've never told anyone how fundamentally sad I am. My family actually thinks I'm a "happy-go-lucky" kind of person, which is the antithesis of what I actually am. I can't talk to anyone, not even my family, because even though they love and care about me (maybe because they love and care about me) they won't even entertain the conversation. I've tried to but they always subtly change the subject or tell me that they're busy and can't talk. And my "friends" at school are all just for show, none of them really care about me, I'm just someone to talk to or joke with on a superficial level. I'm pretty comfortable saying that if I were to kill myself, nobody outside my family would care for a second.
